value.body: Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery. You study anatomy, physiology and other medical basics alongside Ayurveda theory, herbal pharmacology and panchakarma, then complete a one-year internship. It is regulated by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM).

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4½ years of study + 1-year compulsory rotatory internship

items.label: UG seats
items.note: Across ~515 colleges permitted for 2025-26 (list as on 29 Aug 2025); approx. sum
items.source: NCISM list of permitted Ayurveda colleges, approx.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology, and a qualifying NEET-UG score. AACCC (Ministry of Ayush) counsels the 15% All India Quota and central, national-institute and deemed-university seats; states fill the rest through their own counselling.

value.title: At a glance
items: Practice needs registration with a State Board or Council of Indian Medicine.
Roughly four in five permitted Ayurveda colleges are private.
An MD or MS (Ayurveda) through AIAPGET is the usual way to specialise.
